relations: Right hand twisting and pulling its band end causes a knotted twist to form in the horizontal strand.
As the right hand pulls outward, the left thumb withdraws, letting the loop settle around the left index finger.
The right hand maintains tension on the twisted strand, holding the configuration steady against the left index finger.
caption: The video depicts a close-up view over a plain white surface where two hands manipulate a thin, translucent orange elastic band. Two short wooden sticks rest in the background, one angled at the upper left and a smaller piece partly hidden behind the band. The band is held as a small loop pinched between the fingertips of both hands, the left thumb and index finger gripping one side while the right thumb and index finger grip the other. The right hand twists and works its end of the band while the left hand keeps the loop open, so a twisted, knotted section forms in the strand running to the right. As the right hand pulls its end outward, the horizontal strand lengthens and the twist becomes more pronounced, while the left thumb gradually withdraws. The loop then settles around the left index finger, which holds it open, and the right hand's fingertips keep the twisted strand stretched to the right. The configuration is held steady through the rest of the clip with only minor adjustments, the background sticks and white surface staying fixed.
